title: Sukha Singh's Daylight Bath; Mehtab Kot Opens

blocks.text: Sukha Singh carries out his vow by approaching the pool in disguise, letting his horse drink, and then dismounting for the sacred bath. The Mughals were dumbfounded to witness such a scene once his Sikh identity became clear in the very place they had tried to seal off.

Instead of fleeing silently, he raises the Khalsa cry and openly challenges the guards before escaping their fire. The episode presents the bath not as private devotion alone but as a public act of spiritual and political resistance.

By the end of the page, the story turns toward a harsher new campaign against the Singhs. The transition introduces the pressure that will define the Mehtab Kot sequence, where persecution spreads beyond Amritsar into the countryside.
